recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reshape ResearchStudy.title for FHIR-26865; any future status/date metadata, required label.value, or datatype changes for alternate titles should be raised as a new BR&R tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-26865 was a Published/Persuasive R5 BR&R request to support multiple ResearchStudy titles by replacing the single ResearchStudy.title string with a repeating structure carrying title value/name and type for short, long, scientific, and related title use cases.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-26865 was found. The Jira resolution says the request was dealt with under FHIR-31604, and commit d5448ea900e832422a9dfa5dcaea0cd8cb30bb16 implemented FHIR-31604 by adding ResearchStudy.label 0..* with type and value while retaining a singular ResearchStudy.title.
additional_context: ResearchStudy is active in source/fhir.ini. Later decisions confirm the model: FHIR-31901 was retracted after the editor explained that label allows multiple names; FHIR-32312 and FHIR-32975 refined the TitleType values used by label.type; FHIR-37730 approved the current ResearchStudy.title wording; and FHIR-51195 added label.language for translated titles. The 2020 BRR minutes record the original multiple/bilingual-title concern, and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source has ResearchStudy.title as a 0..1 string for the human-readable study name and ResearchStudy.label as a 0..* BackboneElement with type, value, and language, which is the maintained multi-title representation established by FHIR-31604 and later related decisions.
